title: Final project: the kitchen ticket system
story: The kitchen wants a tiny command-driven ticket system. Staff type commands, one per line, and the program responds to each. When the input runs out (the end of the shift), it prints a summary. This brings together input, loops, decisions, functions, dictionaries, lists, errors and string formatting.

requirements.text: It reads commands line by line until the input ends, and ignores blank lines.
`add <pizza> <quantity>` adds a ticket and prints `Ticket <number>: <quantity> x <pizza>`. Tickets are numbered from 1.
`done <number>` marks that ticket done and prints `Ticket <number> done`. A ticket that doesn't exist or is already done prints `No open ticket <number>`.
`open` prints each open ticket as `<number>: <quantity> x <pizza>` in number order, or `Nothing open` if there are none.
Any command that's unknown, has the wrong number of words, or a quantity or number that isn't a whole number above 0, prints `Bad command` and the program carries on.
At the end it prints `Made <n> pizzas` (the total quantity of done tickets), then, if any were made, `Most made: <pizza>`. Ties go to the pizza first alphabetically.

steps: Loop over the input lines until there are none left.
Split each line into words and decide what to do from the first word.
Keep the tickets in a dictionary from number to details.
At the end, total the done tickets and find the most made pizza.
hints: `import sys` then `for line in sys.stdin:` reads every line until the input ends.
Turn quantities into ints inside try/except ValueError, and also check they're above 0.
A dictionary of pizza name to quantity made, plus `min` with a key, finds the winner with ties broken alphabetically.
